Warm-up

Say it the exam way

Light from a galaxy moving away from us is shifted to wavelengths. This is called . The redshift of a galaxy is the change in wavelength divided by the wavelength. Redshift has .

For a slowly moving galaxy, redshift is the ratio of its recessional velocity to the . More distant galaxies are moving away . The Hubble–Lemaître law links recessional velocity and . It lets us estimate the of the Universe.

Answers

Say it the exam way

(1) longer · (2) redshift · (3) rest · (4) no unit · (5) speed of light · (6) faster · (7) distance · (8) age

2019 Paper 1, Question 9: answer B

  • A Not this one. This multiplies v by H0. Rearrange v = H0d to get d = v ÷ H0.
  • B Right. First the speed: v = zc = 0.014 × 3.00 × 108 = 4.2 × 106 m s−1. Then d = v ÷ H0 = 4.2 × 106 ÷ 2.3 × 10−18 = 1.83 × 1024 m.
  • C Not this one. This divides c by H0. The galaxy is not moving at the speed of light. Find its speed first: v = zc.
  • D Not this one. This divides c by z. Redshift is z = v ÷ c, so v = zc, a multiply.
  • E Not this one. This is far too large. Find v = zc first, then divide by H0 once.
